items.text: Hansi Flick has a problem. Injuries have hit his defence, so Frenkie de Jong, a midfielder, will start at centre-back, with Eric García at right-back. Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona. Barça lead La Liga after this round, with 12 wins in 13 games, and Flick has promised attacking football. Then, at minute 5, Villarreal score. At minute 7, they score again. Two goals in 7 minutes. What went wrong at the back, and was Barça already beaten?

Before kick-off, the absences. Barça were without Rodri and 3 more injured players. Villarreal had 4 injured, among them Ilias Akhomach. Form was mixed. Barça had lost to PSG and Real Madrid, then won 3 in a row. Villarreal had lost 6-0 to PSG, then beaten Getafe 2-0. Hansi Flick, before the game, on nine matches in 27 days: "We have a good squad and we need to manage playing time." Íñigo Pérez had a different plan. One Spanish report says he wanted Villarreal to press high, and that defending deep at Camp Nou would not be comfortable.

Flick arrived in May 2024 to replace Xavi. At his presentation, he promised "all possession and really attacking football." Our reading: that promise leans on the back line. Tonight that line has a midfielder at its centre, Frenkie de Jong, with Eric García at right-back. If it cracks, the whole idea is exposed. Ahead of them, Lamine Yamal, the most valuable starter on the pitch at 221 million euros. He is the one asked to make that risk pay.

Minute 5. Fermín López gives the ball away, and Tajon Buchanan scores from distance with his right foot. Minute 7. A fast break, and Tani Oluwaseyi finishes with his left. Two shots, two goals. Early on, it looks like Pérez's plan is working. Then the match tilts. The momentum graph has Barça on top for 77 percent of the first half. Minute 21, Yamal goes down under a challenge from Oluwaseyi. Play goes on, until VAR sends the referee to the monitor. Penalty. Yamal hits the post. Half-time: 0-2.

57 minutes of attack have found nothing. Then one corner. Minute 57. Gerard Martín rises, and heads it in. Minute 61. Fermín López, left foot, from open play. 2-2. Minute 67, Pau Navarro turns the ball into his own net. 3-2. Three goals in 10 minutes. Flick, afterwards: "In the second half, we looked what we want to do better: better structure, a clear structure."

Pedri is the name the numbers pick out. He is rated 9.0, the highest on the pitch, with 6 chances created. There is no running data for La Liga games, so look at the ball: 107 touches and 10 recoveries, his most in his last 6 games. And Fermín López, who gave the ball away for the first goal: 4 goals in his last 4 games, one of them tonight, in 68 minutes on the pitch. Flick put it simply after the match: "If we play like this, the opponent gets tired." Barça had 70 percent of the ball, and 10 corners to Villarreal's none.

Expected goals, or xG, is learned from past shots: distance, angle, foot or head. It says how often a chance like it is scored. Villarreal's two goals were worth 0.04 and 0.06 xG. Almost nothing. Barça's penalty at minute 23 was worth 0.79, and it hit the post. Over the night, Barça finish on 3.29 xG to Villarreal's 0.17. 93 percent of it came through the centre, and many of those shots were blocked. Replay these chances 20,000 times, and Barça win 97 in 100. So the 0-2 half did lie. Barça's chances were not the problem. Luck and finishing were.

Flick, after the match: "We took too long with the ball, made two mistakes and they scored two goals." Then the referee. Fermín, already substituted, protested when no penalty was given for a challenge on Anthony Gordon. The referee's report says he sent Fermín off from the bench at minute 74, and Fermín left before the card was shown. Flick: "We always have this sort of problem with this referee." Barça plan to appeal. A site that rates referees gave him 2.5 out of 10, but says the Yamal penalty was correct.

So, was De Jong the weak point? One report says he was caught out of position for the second goal, leaving Eric García to chase Oluwaseyi. Pedri calls him "extraordinary". The numbers lean his way: 104 of 110 passes, 7 recoveries, 3 of 3 ground duels won, never dribbled past. They cannot show where he stood when that pass was played. Two questions for you. Was De Jong at centre-back a risk worth taking? And was Fermín's red card fair? Tell us in the comments. So what won it? Relentless pressure: 3.29 expected goals to 0.17, and 10 corners to none, until the wall cracked. Stay tuned: the next data breakdown is on its way. Subscribe and hit the bell.

Pedri finished with a 9.0 rating, the highest of anyone on the pitch. He created 6 chances, gave 1 assist and completed 81 of 92 passes. 15 of those passes went into the final third. He also won 7 of his 8 duels. He had 107 touches and 10 recoveries, his most in his last 6 games. The numbers cannot show how he moved without the ball. Does a 9.0 sound fair to you? Full story on the channel.

Barça won 10 corners. Villarreal won none. Villarreal's coach wanted a high press. With 30% of the ball, they ended up defending their own box. At minute 53, a corner gave Marc Bernal a header, and it went wide. At minute 57, another corner gave Gerard Martín a header, and it went in. Four minutes later, Fermín López scored too. The wall had a crack, and Barça kept pushing on it. One caution: 0.79 of the 1.65 set-piece xG was the penalty Yamal hit against the post. So dead balls opened the door, and volume finished the job. Was it the corners or the pressure that won it? Full story on the channel.
